title: Ethiopian Fish Stew
localName: አሣ ወጥ ቀላል — Asa Wet Qelal
community: All of Ethiopia — the everyday fish stew of fasting periods
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Everyday Fish Stew — a simplified fish stew with tomatoes, onions, berbere, and garlic. The quick-cooking fasting-period fish dish that Ethiopian Orthodox Christians prepare during the 200+ annual fasting days. Simple, nutritious, and deeply satisfying.
longDesc: The everyday fish stew is the practical fasting-day meal — simpler than Asa Wat (no dry-caramelisation required), faster, and using whatever fish is available. During Lent and the many other fasting periods, this dish appears on Ethiopian tables across the country.
steps: Cook onions in oil until golden — 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and berbere. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
Add water. Bring to a simmer.
Spoon sauce over fish. Cover. Cook 10—12 minutes.
chefTips: The tomato base must be cooked down before adding fish.
Add lemon with the fish — it brightens and firms the flesh.
commonMistakes: Thin tomato base — diluted by fish water.
cookingScience: See ETH081 for fish stew science.
sustainabilityTips: Any Ethiopian lake fish — supports local fishermen.
culturalNote: Everyday fish stew is the food that sustains Ethiopia's Orthodox Christian majority through 200+ fasting days — the practical, affordable protein that keeps the fast while nourishing the body.
